"It's Windows 9! No, wait! 10!"

They must have done that just to get people talking about it, but there's a hidden self-deprecatory joke there. Every other release of Windows has been terrible. It's a historical pattern with the product name. Windows 9 therefore would have been the one that people love, so they jumped to 10 so we don't get confused and think it's good.

Good marketing, good humor, and good features. I suspect that Balmer had Windows 8 remove so much that we know just so we'd appreciate it when they bring it back. Tricky tricky.
Windows 8.1 was Windows 9. There is logic behind the naming convention, but I forget exactly how it works...

Really, there is no Windows 9 and there can't be due to the bugs it would cause in compatibility shortcut code. The Windows 9 name would trigger procedures designed to run when windows 9x is detected. While MS can use internal version control to get around that in their code, they can't fix the third party software it would break.

Well, there's that, the joke, the marketing, the headlines. There are many reasons to never officially name a release "Windows 9".
